PREAMB.SUBJECT: Procedures To Govern the Use of Satellite Earth Stations on Board Vessels in the 5925-6425 MHz/3700-4200 MHz Bands and 14.0-14.5 GHz/11.7-12.2 GHz Bands

ACT.P: Final rule, announcement of effective date.

SUM.P: This document announces the effective date of the rule published on January 31, 2005. The rules adopted licensing and service rules for satellite earth stations on vessels (ESVs) in the C- and Ku-bands that will provide regulatory certainty to ESV licensees, while protecting existing users in the bands.

FURINF.P: Jennifer Gorny or Howard Griboff, Policy Division, International Bureau, (202) 418-1460.

SUPLINF.P: On January 6, 2005, the Commission released a Report and Order, a summary of which was published in the Federal Register . See 70 FR 4775, January 31, 2005. Although the rule changes in the Report and Order became effective on March 2, 2005, §§ 25.221(c), 25.221(e), and 25.222(c) contained modified information collection requirements, which required approval by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB). The information collection requirements were approved by OMB on May 25, 2005. See OMB No. 3060-1061.

PREAMB.SUBJECT: Determination Related to the Participation of the Magen David Adom Society of Israel in the Activities of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement
PREAMB.P: Pursuant to the requirements contained in the FY 2005 Consolidated Appropriations Act (Division D, Pub. L. 108-447), under the heading of Migration and Refugee Assistance, I hereby determine that the Magen David Adom Society of Israel is not being denied participation in the activities of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement.
This Determination shall be published in the Federal Register , and copies shall be provided to the appropriate committees of the Congress.

SIG.NAME: Condoleeza Rice,
SIG.TITLE: Secretary of State, Department of State.

PREAMB.SUBJECT: Announcement of the Fall 2005 Unsolicited Grant Competition Grant Program

SUM.P: The Agency announces its Upcoming Unsolicited Grant Program, which offers support for research, education and training, and the dissemination of information on international peace and conflict resolution. The Unsolicited competition is open to any project that falls within the Institute's broad mandate of international conflict resolution.

Deadline: October 1, 2005. Application Material Available on
Request and at http://www.usip.org/grants.
